skill.name: verify-task-funding
skill.description: Verify whether an online bounty, freelance task, agent marketplace job, hackathon prize, or crypto work offer is actually open, accessible, and credibly funded. Use when evaluating task URLs, payout claims, escrow or treasury evidence, eligibility restrictions, payment history, expected value, or whether a claimed amount may be counted as real revenue.
skill.summary: Verify funding, eligibility, payment conditions, and expected value before accepting online work.
skill.author: geiccobs

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown links, inline code formatting, and explicit warnings against exposing credentials. Two external links create low network and payment-flow risk. The unsupported safety-review claim and publisher-controlled paid-service promotion require marketplace disclosure and remediation.

remediation.issue: The README describes an external listing as safety-reviewed without evidence in the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the safety claim or link to a verifiable, current audit with its scope, date, and reviewer.

remediation.issue: The skill promotes publisher-controlled paid services within its operational instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Separate promotions from the skill workflow and disclose ownership, pricing, data handling, and alternatives before any referral.

remediation.issue: A paid API and marketplace link can expose user data or lead to a USDC transaction.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before contacting either service or initiating payment, and explain all charges before use.

content.user_title: Verify Task Funding Before You Commit
content.value_statement: Online work offers often hide weak funding, closed access, or costly payout conditions. This skill reviews primary evidence and estimates conservative expected value before you commit.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a task appears open and accepts applications or submissions.
Reviews geography, identity, wallet network, and account eligibility requirements.
Ranks funding evidence from confirmed receipt through unsupported claims.
Distinguishes advertised payout from funded, withdrawable, and received value.
Estimates expected net value using payment probability, fees, spending, and labor.
Returns a conservative classification with evidence links, red flags, and recommended action.
limitations: Cannot guarantee that a sponsor, platform, or contract will pay.
Depends on accessible, current, and authentic primary evidence.
Cannot confirm private balances or documents that the user does not provide.
Optional external checks may charge fees and require separate user approval.

use_cases.title: Screen a Freelance Offer
use_cases.description: Review payout terms, eligibility, fees, and payment history before investing unpaid labor.

use_cases.title: Assess a Crypto Bounty
use_cases.description: Verify escrow, wallet network, withdrawal conditions, and required spending before accepting a bounty.

use_cases.title: Compare Prize Opportunities
use_cases.description: Compare funding strength and expected net value across hackathons or marketplace tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task URL: [URL]. Confirm whether it is open, eligible, and credibly funded. List evidence, red flags, and your recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a quick assessment of one opportunity.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Payout Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the payout claim for [task]. Separate advertised value, escrow, withdrawable funds, and received revenue. Cite primary evidence and state uncertainties.
prompt_templates.scenario: A worker wants to understand the strength of a payout claim.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Expected Value
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [task URL] using payout, payment probability, fees, required spending, labor hours, and hourly value. Show assumptions and estimate expected net value.
prompt_templates.scenario: A professional needs an economic decision before starting work.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these opportunities: [URLs]. Verify status, eligibility, funding, payment conditions, competition, costs, and expected net value. Rank them by evidence quality.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user is allocating time across several paid opportunities.

output_examples.input: Review a bounty advertising 2,000 USDC with no visible escrow and discretionary acceptance.
output_examples.output: Classification: CONDITIONAL. The advertised payout is not task-funded, and payment depends on acceptance. Verify sponsor history before committing substantial work.

output_examples.input: Assess a hackathon page whose submission deadline passed yesterday.
output_examples.output: Classification: CLOSED_OR_INELIGIBLE. The submission window is closed, so the prize should not be treated as an available opportunity.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a platform balance marked available, with documented withdrawal fees and supported geography.
output_examples.output: Classification: WITHDRAWABLE. The balance appears available under documented terms, but it is not realized revenue until receipt is confirmed.

best_practices: Provide the canonical task URL, exact payout claim, deadline, and relevant eligibility details.
Prefer task-specific escrow, explorer records, platform releases, and official terms over marketing claims.
Keep facts, assumptions, unknowns, and estimates clearly separated.
anti_patterns: Do not treat total prize pools or sponsor reputation as task-specific funding.
Do not count pending, conditional, promotional, or withdrawable balances as received revenue.
Do not share credentials, private keys, seed phrases, or authentication tokens.

faq.question: Can this skill guarantee payment?
faq.answer: No. It assesses available evidence and payment conditions, but counterparties and platforms can still fail.

faq.question: What evidence is strongest?
faq.answer: Confirmed receipt is strongest, followed by withdrawable balances, task-specific escrow, and official funded award records.

faq.question: Does an advertised prize prove funding?
faq.answer: No. Marketing copy, total prize pools, and sponsor reputation do not prove that a specific task is funded.

faq.question: Can it evaluate crypto bounties?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review on-chain funding, escrow, wallet networks, withdrawal terms, fees, and payment history.

faq.question: Does the skill require a paid service?
faq.answer: No. The core workflow is free. Any external paid check requires separate review and explicit user approval.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the task URL, payout claim, deadline, location, account constraints, estimated effort, and any available funding evidence.
